chunks: It is He who grew the gardens, trellised and bowered, and palm trees and land sown with corn and many other seeds, and olives and pomegranates, alike and yet unlike. So eat of their fruit when they are in fruit, and give on the day of harvesting His due, and do not be extravagant, for God does not love those who are prodigal.

key_terms.لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْرِفِينَ: He does not love the extravagant/wasteful

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of giving the 'due' at harvest time and avoiding extravagance in Islamic teachings?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the 'due' (haqquhu) is often interpreted as a specific agricultural tithe or zakat, emphasizing the spiritual responsibility of stewardship over natural resources. The distinction between varied and similar fruits highlights divine wisdom in creating diversity, while the prohibition of 'israf' (extravagance) serves as a moral guideline for sustainable consumption and economic justice.
